corrections.compiler_and_flags: setup.py builds the C extension with -O3 -Wall -Wextra (compiler unstated); flags for the README table run are not stated
corrections.caveats: First-party README table with no hardware, compiler, zstd level or benchmark script for the single-thread numbers; the table is for v0.2.0 (current 0.5.4) and labels zstd 'v1.56'. The C Huffman coder is not ZipNN's own: setup.py compiles Yann Collet's FiniteStateEntropy (huf_compress.c, huf_decompress.c, fse_*.c vendored under include/FiniteStateEntropy) and csrc/zipnn_core.c calls HUF_compress/HUF_decompress, i.e. the same Huffman family zstd uses for literals. The win over zstd comes from byte grouping (separating bfloat16 exponent bytes) plus Huffman-only coding, so the entropy-coder contribution is not isolated; category fit for entropy-coders is weak (domain-specific lossless compressor for model weights). Default configuration is byte grouping of 4 with vanilla zstd; method 'auto' picks zstd, lz4 or huffman. The LICENSE.txt is MIT but its copyright line names IBM and 'the Drain3 project contributors' (boilerplate copied from another IBM project). Peer-reviewed paper (IEEE CLOUD 2025, arXiv 2411.05239) not opened: blocked here.

notes: Numbers match README exactly; 1.4x/1.7x ratios check out (1120/785, 1660/950). Recommend a decision category override to general-lossless (baseline zstd, transform plus vendored FSE HUF), or keep in entropy-coders with the shortcoming recorded. Paper-access retier candidate (IEEE CLOUD 2025) for B.
